Subject: Questions on retention floor vs redaction options for PHI/PII

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Security want a short note on two items so our legal team can scope the contract:

1) Retention floor: our regulators insist on a minimum retention window for auditability in some scenarios. We need to understand what "retention floor" options you support (tenant-level, account-level, customer-specified) and how they interact with automatic purges.

2) Field sanitization / redaction: if we ask Redwood to redact PHI fields post-ingest, what guarantees do we have (irreversibility, logs, audit trail)? Also: how do you handle partial redaction vs tokenization for downstream model performance?

Can you send a short implementation matrix (options, tradeoffs, estimated delivery effort) and any reference playbook? We have a procurement review on Thursday 10/15 and would like a one-pager by 10/12.

Appreciate it —
Emily
Emily Park

Subject: Re: Questions on retention floor vs redaction options for PHI/PII

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick answer up front: we support configurable retention floors at tenant and account scope, plus field-level redaction and irreversible deletion workflows with audit trails. The tradeoffs are mainly around retrieval/export requirements and downstream model quality when heavy redaction is applied.

I attached an outline I put together (redaction_playbook_outline.pdf) and a rough mutual action plan (ma_plan.xlsx) that maps milestones to delivery effort. Quick highlights:
- Tenant-level retention floor: low effort to configure, covers all data but may conflict with customer-specific shorter deletion requests.
- Account-scoped retention windows: more flexible, recommended for multi-tenant customers who want mix of retention policies.
- Field sanitization: we offer deterministic redaction (regex/field mapping) and irreversible zeroization. Deterministic redaction retains schema but replaces values; zeroization removes or overwrites tokens and writes an immutable audit event.

Questions for you to help scope the one-pager: do you require export of pre-redaction data for audits? Any preservation exceptions (legal hold, clinical research) we should account for?

I'll loop in Priyom for implementation timing and Monica for compliance language.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Rafael — that helps. A few clarifications:
- We will likely require export of pre-redaction records for audit teams for a rolling 90-day window; after that exports should not contain raw identifiers unless legally necessary.
- Legal hold: occasional preservation required for litigation; we need the option to flag specific tenants/records from deletion even if retention policy would otherwise purge.
- For downstream models: we care that redaction doesn’t break routing/metadata — e.g., if we remove SSNs but still want classification labels that rely on masked tokens.

If you can include the preservation-exception flow and an example of irreversible deletion audit entries, that would be ideal for the 10/12 one-pager.

Emily

Rafael/Monica — quick implementation notes from infra/solutions:

- Tenant vs account retention: we can expose a retention-floor API and an override API for preservation flags. Estimated work: 2 sprint cycle (4 weeks) to make the policy UI + API GA-ready; 1 additional week for tenant migration/build docs.
- Export path: we can provide an export endpoint that returns pre-redaction artifacts for a configurable retention window (default 90 days) and writes an immutable export job entry to the audit log. That export job will be encrypted and access-controlled.
- Irreversible deletion: two-step flow (request + confirmation) that triggers zeroization of KV cache and metadata sweep; we will emit an audit event with a deletion-hash and timestamp. Recovery is only possible if an explicit legal-hold snapshot was taken prior to zeroization.

Open items for legal/compliance: examples of acceptable export retention windows, acceptable evidence retention format (PDF vs. JSON), and whether audit logs need to be retained off-platform.

Priyom

Rafael/Priyom/Emily — agreed positions for the one-pager and legal language:

- Definitive statement: "Redwood provides configurable retention floors and irreversible deletion mechanisms. Irreversible deletion is performed only after an explicit delete workflow and emits an immutable audit event; recovery requires a pre-deletion legal hold snapshot."
- Preservation/Legal hold: we will include a customer-controlled preservation flag that supersedes scheduled purges until the flag is cleared. We recommend customers capture an export snapshot before clearing a legal hold.
- Redaction guarantees: deterministic redaction (masking) is reversible only if the customer stores a separate token map under their control; irreversible zeroization is not reversible. We should offer both and document model degradation risk for heavy redaction in the runbook.
- Sample audit entry (for the playbook): "DELETION_EVENT | tenant=ns-prod | object_id=12345 | method=zeroize | audit_hash=sha256:abc... | timestamp=2026-10-09T09:27:00Z"

I'll draft the one-pager language and share a short compliance appendix covering export formats and log retention guidance. Rafael — can you confirm the delivery timeline for the 1-pager (10/12) and the technical runbook (10/22)?

Monica Patel
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
